source_scope.paper: GraSP: Graph-Structured Skill Compositions for LLM Agents

findings.claim: GraSP is a verified skill-execution design: retrieved skills are compiled into a dependency DAG, nodes have precondition checks and postcondition verification, and failed nodes can trigger local repair rather than blindly advancing the graph.
findings.scope_guard: Architecture evidence only; this does not by itself isolate the causal effect of verifier checks.

findings.claim: On ScienceWorld, GraSP reports 84.9 versus 81.5 without DAG compilation, 82.9 without local repair, and 81.8 with global replan. However, the published ablations jointly alter dependency tracking/partial execution or repair policy; there is no verification-only ablation holding the retrieved skill identity and other graph machinery fixed.
findings.scope_guard: Do not attribute the 3.4-point w/o-DAG gap or the 2.0-point w/o-local-repair gap solely to pre/postcondition verification, and do not treat them as fixed-selected-identity receiver acceptance causality.

protocol_implication.name: VERIFIER_COMPONENT_ATTRIBUTION_GUARD
protocol_implication.rule: A per-node verifier may be part of a strong science-agent architecture, but a causal verifier claim requires an ablation that preserves retrieved identity, graph/dependency representation, repair policy, state and execution budget while toggling only the verifier/admission decision.
